newsitem.title: FRANCE: French homeless fail overturn Riviera begging ban.
newsitem.headline: French homeless fail overturn Riviera begging ban.

text.p: The homeless of Nice have lost a legal bid to overturn a summertime ban on begging in the centre of the French Riviera capital, their lawyer said on Thursday.

Lawyer Joseph Ciccolini said the Nice public prosecutor had thrown out charges that the municipality had violated the rights of 26 people by detaining them, questioning them and dumping them at a hostel 16 km (10 miles) out of town with no transport.
Ciccolini said the prosecutors' office, which asked the police to investigate the allegations, ruled there was insufficient evidence.

"The questions posed by these complaints are still unanswered," he said, adding he would start a different legal procedure in coming days against the by-law. The 26 alleged they were victims of "restrictions on individual liberty".

Several French towns have banned beggars in the summer tourist season, embarrassing the centre-right government which says it is fighting for the poor and homeless. Prime Minister Alain Juppe has branded such by-laws "municipal egoism".

Right-wing Nice Mayor Jacques Peyrat won a referendum on the ban in November when voters approved it by a two-to-one margin. But turnout was a dismal 20 percent. A total of 1,356 homeless people were forcibly evicted from the town under the system.
